reviews.author: Rakie Kim
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Rakie Kim noted that the original patch description was misleading due to their own misunderstanding of the series' intent, which led them to think it was about adding per-socket per-node weights instead of restricting existing weights.

Rakie Kim noted that their initial misunderstanding of the patch series was due to confusion between this work and another discussion from 2025, where a 2-D grid with weights per-node, per-CPU was proposed.

Rakie Kim noted that the original patch description was unclear and suggested rephrasing it as 'Respect the initiator's point of view' to better convey the goal of the series.

Reviewer Rakie Kim noted that the patch is hard to review due to its large size and suggested splitting it into smaller patches for easier understanding.

Rakie Kim suggested adding documentation about the new interface in both the cover letter and kernel documentation, aiming at operators.

Reviewer Rakie Kim noted that the DDR generation is the same across DRAM and CXL, but the difference in results comes from the path rather than the memory itself, and suggested clarifying this point when describing the system.

Rakie Kim suggested changing the demotion order to be based on packages instead of sockets, indicating that this is a natural first step and expressing willingness to investigate further once the placement side has settled.

Reviewer Rakie Kim noted that the original patch description was unclear and caused them to misunderstand the intent of the series, but after clarification, they are supportive of the goal to make the weighted interleave mechanism respect the initiator's point of view.

Rakie Kim noted that the original patch was too large and complex due to multiple features being included, and requested that it be split into smaller patches for easier review.

Reviewer Rakie Kim suggested splitting the large patch (2/4) into smaller patches to make it easier for reviewers, citing that a 1k line patch is hard to review in its entirety.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, 12 Aug 2026 07:49:55 -0700 Joshua Hahn <joshua.hahnjy@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello Joshua,

Thank you for coming back to this so quickly.

---

My explanation was not enough and that is what caused the confusion.
The 2-D grid is close enough to this work that the two are easy to
place together, and thanks to your questions I could fill in a good
deal of what the cover letter was missing.

---

Thank you. "Respect the initiator's point of view" describes the goal
better than what I wrote, so I would like to use that framing in the
next cover letter.

---

Agreed. I will also keep thinking about what such use cases would
look like.

---

I will put it in both. Andrew also asked for documentation aimed at
the operator, so the next version will describe this interface and
how to use it there as well.

---

Both sides are DDR5-6400, so the difference in the results comes from
the path rather than from the memory itself. I will make that clear
when I describe the system in the next version.

---

Thank you for the suggestion. Changing the demotion order by package
sounds like the natural first step, and I will look into it once the
placement side has settled.

---

Thank you for saying so. Either way, your questions gave me a chance
to look again at what the cover letter was not saying clearly.

---

You are right, it is too much to take in at once. The patch became
large and complex because several features ended up in a single
commit. I will separate them as much as I can in the next version.

---

Thank you again for the review and for the discussion. I hope you
have a great day too.

Rakie Kim

2026-08-13.patch_summary: This patch series introduces package-aware weighted interleave, which modifies the existing weighted interleave mechanism to respect the initiator's point of view when making memory allocations. The goal is to simplify user configuration and improve performance by reducing cross-socket memory movements. The approach involves adding a restriction to the existing weights, rather than introducing new per-socket or per-node weights as initially misunderstood. This change aims to promote socket-local memory allocation and demote cross-socket allocations, potentially eliminating the need for explicit NUMAB2 promotions. The patch series consists of four patches, with one being particularly large (1k lines) and suggested to be split into smaller patches for easier review.
